messages.subject: Javascript and Shiny integration
parts:
Hi,

I'm studying how to join shiny and javascript/jquery,
and I've created this simple code on gist: https://gist.github.com/anonymous/6629268
How can I call the js function color on each dataset change??

Thanks

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: Javascript and Shiny integration
parts:
I assume the code is just for demonstration, since you can just override default css styles to change cell background without javascript.
Given your dataset is a reactive dataset() you can call for a js function with session$sendCustomMessage. Like so:
observe({
    if (!is.null(dataset()))
        session$sendCustomMessage(
            type = "myType",
            message = list(**can pass agruments here**)
        )
})

Your js would be like
$(document).ready(function() {
  Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("myType",
    function(message){
       /*do stuff here*/
    }
  );
})

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: Javascript and Shiny integration
parts:
Yeah, as far as I understand, you can change priorities of observers, but not outputs like renderTable.
What are you trying to achieve? If you just want to change cell background colors, use includeCSS('tables.css') where table.css containing something like #mytable td{background-color: #CCC}
You can also:
- Send raw data to your js through sendCustomMessage and generate table in javascript. You'll have to destroy table in a given div and place a new one with each data update.
or
- Generate table tags in R and pass them to renderText() like I've done here.

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: Javascript and Shiny integration
parts:
Try this

https://gist.github.com/xiaodaigh/6662247

I have change dyour color.js to use delegate. Basically your code didn't run because Shiny creates the table then you apply css to it. Check jQuery documentation http://api.jquery.com/delegate/

With delegates, you tell the browser to look for a table with id mytable and whenever it's content is changed it runs color. Not sure what the Javascript jargon is but I think it might the event is delegated/attached to the document.

This is a great solution.. however, I ran into an issue.
I am outputting a carousel using bxslider. After I output the div (using renderText), I have to call $('.carousels').bxSlider();

I tried to you use the delegate solution to call bxSlider() once the div has been rendered, however calling that changes the div itself, which triggers that event and ends up calling the bxSlider() in an infinite loop.
In your example, I see that you just modified the css background in your function. I don't know why that does not trigger the delegate function. But calling bxSlider() does.

The end result I want is that once the carousel is rendered, something calls bxSlider() to make it a proper carousel. What is the best way to do that?

Any help would be appreciated.
